statement: The system shall make number porting faster and more reliable.
The system shall keep all providers synchronized on the same source of truth.
The system shall validate requests quickly.
The system shall activate routing changes on time.
The system shall minimize errors and manual reconciliations.
The system shall keep turnaround time short from request submission to completion.
The system shall maintain high accuracy in matching and updating portability data.
The system shall comply with regulatory and audit requirements.
The system shall reduce back-and-forth between providers.
The system shall reduce the time operations teams spend coordinating exceptions and allow them to focus on true conflicts or exceptions.
The system shall support operations staff from participating telecom providers as users.
The system shall support a central administration or NPAC-style operations team that oversees the process.
Provider users shall be able to submit porting data.
Provider users shall be able to receive porting data.
Provider users shall be able to check request status.
Provider users shall be able to respond to conflicts.
Provider users shall be able to correct records for their own company.
The central administration team shall validate transactions.
The central administration team shall manage exceptions.
The central administration team shall trigger routing updates.
The central administration team shall monitor the shared data set.
The system shall provide read-only access for auditors or compliance users.
Auditors or compliance users shall have access to history and traceability.
Auditors or compliance users shall not be able to change transactions.
The system shall capture the gaining provider’s port request and the losing provider’s information when a port starts.
The system shall validate the port request details.
The system shall check whether the number is eligible for porting.
The system shall verify that the records from both providers match before any activation occurs.
The system shall place the port request into a conflict state when there is a mismatch or dispute.
The system shall keep the port request in conflict state until the providers resolve the issue or the operations team intervenes.
The system shall schedule or trigger the routing update once the request is approved.
The system shall distribute the new portability data to all participating networks once the request is approved.
The system shall close the transaction as completed after activation.
The system shall maintain a full audit trail of who submitted the request, who approved it, what changed, and when each step happened.
The system shall enforce the cutoffs and completion deadlines required by applicable regulatory rules and operational agreements.
The system shall configure timing rules centrally as data rather than hardcoding them.
The system shall allow timing rules to vary by jurisdiction and regulator.
The system shall allow timing rules to vary by provider group or process type when needed.
The system shall apply the appropriate rule set based on the port's context.
The system shall allow one transaction to follow a different deadline than another without custom development.
Authorized users shall be able to update cutoffs through administration screens.
Authorized users shall be able to update business days through administration screens.
Authorized users shall be able to update holidays through administration screens.
Authorized users shall be able to update SLA windows through administration screens.
Authorized users shall be able to update exception handling rules through administration screens.
Authorized users shall not be able to change the core validation logic itself.
The system shall notify the gaining and losing provider operational contacts first when a porting request requires notification.
The system shall alert the central operations team when a porting request deadline is at risk.
The system shall alert the central operations team when a porting request enters a conflict state.
The system shall provide in-app alerts for users working directly in the system.
The system shall use email for broader visibility and after-hours follow-up.
The system shall support SMS for urgent escalations.
The system shall support automated integration messages to provider systems for urgent escalations.
The system shall support shared administration and coordination functions for number portability between providers.
The system shall include validation functions for number portability between providers.
The system shall include routing update functions for number portability between providers.
The system shall include synchronization functions for number portability between providers.
The system shall provide operational controls around history for number portability between providers.
The system shall provide operational controls around conflicts for number portability between providers.
The system shall provide operational controls around reporting for number portability between providers.
The system shall provide operational controls around audit for number portability between providers.
The system shall handle exceptions.
The system shall allow involved providers and internal teams to track what happened.
The current process for coordinating number portability requests is manual and fragmented.
Number portability requests are received from both the losing provider and the gaining provider through separate channels.
Operations staff perform a large amount of validation on number portability requests.
The process reconciles the submitted details for number portability requests.
The process resolves mismatches or conflicts in the submitted details.
The process pushes routing updates to the participating networks after reconciliation and conflict resolution.
The process depends heavily on staff coordination and timely data updates.
Traceability is an ongoing pain point in the current process.
Synchronization is an ongoing pain point in the current process.
The system shall automate as much of request validation and coordination as possible.
The system shall reduce the number of cases requiring manual intervention.
The system shall provide a single system of record for transaction history.
The system shall provide a single system of record for conflict handling.
The system shall provide a single system of record for audit trails.
The system shall provide better reporting.
The system shall make pending portability actions more clear.
The system shall make completed portability actions more clear.
The system shall make failed portability actions more clear.
The system shall distribute updated portability data reliably to all participating networks.
The system shall provide operational alerts or exception notifications when something fails or a request gets stuck.
The system shall provide clear role-based access control so that only the appropriate people can approve exceptions or release routing changes.
The system shall capture the approval trail for exceptions or routing changes in the audit history.
The system shall support a second review or escalation path for sensitive actions when a request is disputed or outside normal rules.
The system shall keep provider records synchronized as part of updates.
The system shall work reliably.
The system shall reduce manual effort right away.
The system shall provide a foundation for conflict handling.
The system shall provide approvals after the initial foundation is delivered.
The system shall provide reporting after the initial foundation is delivered.
The system shall check that request data from the losing and gaining providers matches.
The system shall check that the number is eligible to be ported.
The system shall check that the request follows the required business rules before any approval is granted.
If there is a mismatch or missing information, the system shall flag the issue and route it to operations instead of allowing automatic progression.
The system shall coordinate the handoff between providers so the routing change occurs only after the request is fully validated.
The system shall verify whether the number already has a pending porting request as part of the eligibility check.
The system shall verify whether there are any obvious blocks that make the number ineligible to move as part of the eligibility check.
The system shall confirm that required fields are present as part of the business-rule checks.
The system shall confirm that the request timing is valid as part of the business-rule checks.
If any eligibility or business-rule checks fail, the system shall stop the transaction and show a clear reason so operations knows what to fix.
The system shall support a pending transaction state.
The system shall support a validated transaction state.
The system shall support an approved transaction state.
The system shall support a failed transaction state.
The system shall support a completed transaction state.
The system shall support a disputed transaction state.
The system shall support rejected or cancelled transaction states.
The system shall provide a clear way for operations to close out rejected or cancelled cases.
Each transaction state shall be unambiguous and visible in the history.
The system shall support operations staff in handling exceptions.
The system shall support operations staff in handling disputes.
The system shall support operations staff in day-to-day monitoring.
The system shall consider input from participating providers.
The system shall consider input from people who submit porting requests.
The system shall consider input from people who approve porting requests.
The system shall satisfy compliance or audit stakeholder requirements for access control.
The system shall satisfy compliance or audit stakeholder requirements for traceability.
The system shall satisfy compliance or audit stakeholder requirements for reporting.
The system shall reduce delays.
The system shall provide clear auditability from the start.
The shared service shall provide good performance.
The shared service shall provide high availability.
The shared service shall be available during business hours and change windows because providers depend on it.
The system shall support solid error recovery.
If a distribution update or routing update fails, the system shall allow the transaction to be picked up again without losing the transaction state.
A customer may port a phone number when moving service from one telecommunications provider to another while keeping the same number.
A customer may port a number when consolidating services, changing between mobile and fixed service, or moving a number between brands or network partners within the portability environment.
The system shall support number porting in a way that completes the move cleanly and accurately without interrupting service longer than necessary.
The system shall keep the old provider, the new provider, and the shared portability data synchronized during number porting.
The system shall coordinate the handoff, validate that the porting request is legitimate, and update routing so calls and messages go to the correct network.
The new provider shall submit the port request and act as the main driver of the number porting process.
The old provider shall review the port request and accept or reject it based on customer data and any outstanding issues.
The shared administration system shall validate the port request.
The shared administration system shall track the transaction status.
The shared administration system shall coordinate timing.
The shared administration system shall ensure both sides work from the same portability records.
The new provider shall retain responsibility for confirming the customer’s intent.
The new provider shall retain responsibility for preparing the activation.
The old provider shall retain responsibility for checking eligibility.
The old provider shall retain responsibility for identifying any conflicts or discrepancies.
The old provider shall retain responsibility for releasing the number once the port is approved.
The system shall support participating roles beyond the donating and receiving providers.
The system shall support a central administration or portability operator role.
The system shall support network or carrier participants that consume updated routing data but are not directly involved in the portability request.
The system shall provide these roles with updated portability information so their routing remains aligned.
The system shall support nationwide coverage across all participating regions.
Number portability shall work consistently regardless of where the number originates or terminates.
The system shall handle traffic bursts during business hours, end-of-month cycles, and campaign periods.
The system shall handle bursts without delaying validation or routing updates.
The shared system shall accommodate different daily processing windows for different carriers.
The shared system shall respect carrier processing windows and shall not force activation outside those windows.
The shared system shall accommodate cutoff times for same-day processing versus next-day processing.
Carrier cutoff times shall affect when a request can move from validation to approval and then to routing activation.
Submission is the point when the port request is first sent into the shared system by the new provider.
Validation means checking the request details against the system's records for the number, customer, and provider data to ensure the request is complete and eligible.
Approval is the point when the old provider has accepted the request and the port can proceed.
Routing activation or cutover is the actual switch that updates traffic so the number points to the new provider's network.
Routing activation or cutover must occur only within the allowed timing window.
A porting request shall be treated as the formal transaction opened to move one or more numbers from the old provider to the new provider for a specific customer.
A portability record shall be treated as the authoritative data entry kept for each number or transaction so all participants can see its current status, ownership history, and routing state.
The migration process shall be controlled and auditable from the beginning.
The old data shall be carefully mapped into the new system to preserve transaction history and current routing status.
Migrated records shall be validated against the source data.
The migration process shall include a reconciliation step to catch mismatches before go-live.
The new system shall become the system of record at cutover.
The old records shall be retained for reference and dispute handling after cutover.
Unclear source data shall be flagged for manual review rather than automatically overwritten.
The portability system shall support the telecommunications portability regulations that apply in the jurisdiction.
The portability system shall support timely processing of portability requests in accordance with applicable regulations.
The portability system shall support accurate routing in accordance with applicable regulations.
The portability system shall maintain evidence of who approved each action and when.
The system shall preserve transaction and audit records for the required retention period.
The system shall enforce access controls so that only authorized staff can view sensitive portability data.
The system shall provide reporting support for compliance checks.
The system shall include standardized regulatory report content such as request counts, completion times, failures, dispute cases, and status breakdowns.
The system shall generate regulatory reports in the specific template or file type prescribed by the regulator.
The system shall support alternative report formats for ad hoc audits, internal management reporting, and one-off regulator extraction requests.
The exact mandatory regulatory report format must be confirmed against the regulator’s current reporting rules.
The system shall store carrier-specific cutoff rules for each stage.
Some providers shall accept new submissions only until a certain cutoff time, and submissions received after that time shall roll to the next business day.
For pending reviews and approvals, the system shall respect whether a carrier processes them continuously or only within a defined business window.
For activation, the system shall follow the carrier’s allowed activation window and any same-day versus next-day rule tied to the request timestamp and approval time.
The system shall reflect carrier window changes for holidays or exceptional maintenance without requiring manual overrides for every transaction.
The system shall create a record as soon as the submission is accepted into the system.

Once the request is approved, and especially once routing activation is scheduled or executed, the record shall become tightly controlled so that only authorized changes or cancellation actions can occur.
If there is a rollback, rejection, or cancellation, the system shall not erase the original record.
The system shall keep a full audit trail of what happened, when it happened, and why.
The system shall capture failed validation events.
The system shall capture carrier rejection events.
The system shall capture missed cutoff events.
The system shall capture conflicting request events.
The system shall capture activation failure events.
The system shall capture cancellation events.
The system shall capture rollback events.
The system shall capture manual intervention events.
Exception records shall allow operations to see exactly where the request stopped.
Depending on the event, the request shall pause for correction.
Depending on the event, the request shall move into a terminal failed state.
The system shall preserve the original request data.
The system shall preserve resolution notes.
The system shall flag the request as discrepant or awaiting correction.
The system shall keep the request out of the normal approval flow until the mismatch is resolved.
The system shall record the mismatch details.
The system shall record who identified the mismatch.
The system shall record any revised submission or confirmation returned from the providers.
Once the correction is accepted, the system shall move the request back into the normal process state.
The system shall keep the history of the discrepancy attached to the record.
If the mismatch cannot be resolved, the system shall close the request as failed or canceled with a clear reason code.
The system shall block true duplicate portability requests rather than let them proceed.
The system shall warn the operator and prevent a new portability submission from proceeding if it matches an existing open request until the prior case is resolved or explicitly closed.
The system shall treat a portability request as a duplicate when the same telephone number is already in an open or pending portability case.
The duplicate-matching rule may also consider a portability request a duplicate when the customer or account reference and service address match closely enough to indicate the same port.
If an existing request is still active for the same number, the system should reject a new request rather than queue it.
The system should treat different stages as still allowing only one live port path for the same number.
The system may link an attempted submission to the existing case as a related event.
The system should not create a second independent workflow for the same number while an existing request is active.
If the earlier request is in a terminal state such as closed, canceled, or failed, the system can accept a new request normally.
The rules should explicitly define the exact handling by stage.
The default rule should allow only one active request per number at any time.
The system shall not auto-load incomplete, conflicting, or unmappable source records as if they were clean.
The system shall flag incomplete, conflicting, or unmappable source records for manual review.
The system shall preserve the source data as-is for incomplete, conflicting, or unmappable source records.
The system shall hold incomplete, conflicting, or unmappable source records in an exception queue or exclude them from cutover until the mapping issue is resolved.
If a conflict cannot be resolved in time, the business shall decide whether to defer the affected subset, load it with a known exception status, or leave it out and reconcile it afterward.
The system shall not allow bad migration data to contaminate the active portability records.
The system shall define the core validation and retention rules now.
The system shall allow the finer reconciliation workflow to remain open for now if the team still needs to agree on operational details.
The system shall retain the original import evidence for audit.
The minimum rule shall be clear enough to support testing and to prove what was accepted, what was rejected, and why.

A portability record shall become effectively immutable once it has been approved, especially after routing has been activated, except for tightly controlled correction fields or an authorized amendment process.
Only designated operations users shall be able to change a portability record after approval and routing activation, and such changes shall be subject to strong audit tracking.
When a portability record is changed after approval and routing activation, the system shall retain the prior version rather than overwrite it.

If a portability record is corrected later, the system shall keep the full change history, the reason for the amendment, who approved it, and any source evidence or provider confirmation tied to the correction.
The system shall support per-network configuration for distributing updates.
Each participating network may use a different exchange format or transport protocol.
The system shall use each network's agreed interface for update exchange.
The system shall use a network's agreed interface only if it meets the required security and delivery standards.
If a network cannot accept the preferred update method, the system shall not drop the update.
If a network cannot accept the preferred update method, the system shall queue the update.
If a network cannot accept the preferred update method, the system shall retry delivery.
If a network cannot accept the preferred update method, the system shall alert operations so they can switch to an approved fallback or resolve the interface issue.
The system shall provide a clear exception path for update delivery failures.
The system shall pause automated updates for a network when the agreed interface does not meet the required security or delivery standards.
The system shall move the exchange to an approved alternate channel if one exists.
If no preapproved alternate channel exists, the system shall require manual intervention before any data is released.
The system shall not send portability data through an untrusted path.
Operations shall be alerted immediately when the fallback is triggered.
The network liaison or support team should also be alerted to coordinate the fix with the participant.
If the issue affects multiple networks or the main distribution service, the broader service management and audit teams should be notified.
The exact protocol choices and fallback mappings shall be finalized when each network’s interface agreement is confirmed.
If needed after an exception, staff shall use a manual or alternate path.
Staff shall be alerted after repeated failures or if the message is malformed in a way that cannot be auto-corrected.
The system shall not trigger an alert on the first failed attempt.
The system shall continue retry processing quietly for transient failures.
The system shall escalate any issue that could affect service continuity right away.
The administration console shall allow operations staff to review incoming provider requests.
The administration console shall allow operations staff to check validation results.
The administration console shall allow operations staff to resolve exceptions or conflicts.
The administration console shall allow authorized operations staff to approve or correct records.
The administration console shall allow operations staff to monitor the status of routing updates and network distributions.
The administration console shall allow operations staff to search transaction history.
The administration console shall allow operations staff to generate reports.
The administration console shall allow operations staff to review audit trails when something needs to be explained later.
The administration console shall provide a clear status view.
The administration console shall provide fast search.
The administration console shall provide obvious exception handling with minimal steps to complete common actions.
The administration console shall not be cluttered.
The administration console shall support routine work without requiring users to jump between screens.
The administration console shall clearly separate alerts and approvals from informational items.
The administration console shall provide straightforward on-screen guidance for users.
The administration console shall provide clear labels.
The administration console shall provide workflow prompts so newer staff can understand what to do without memorizing every rule.
The administration console shall support role-based access.
The administration console shall provide a simpler default view.
The administration console shall make more advanced functions available only to trained users.
The administration console shall include searchable help or quick reference guidance.
Before accepting a provider portability request, the console shall check that all required provider and customer identifiers are present.
Before accepting a provider portability request, the console shall verify that the number is eligible for portability.
Before accepting a provider portability request, the console shall validate that the request matches the expected format and authorization rules.
Before accepting a provider portability request, the console shall validate that the request is not a duplicate and is not in conflict with an existing pending or completed transaction.
If validation fails or required information is missing, the console shall reject the submission with a clear reason and tell the user what needs to be corrected.
If the issue is minor and can be edited, the console may keep the request in a draft or correction state.
The console shall not enter a request into the active processing flow until it passes validation.
The console shall distinguish missing required fields from other validation failures.
The console shall distinguish format or data-quality errors from other validation failures.
The console shall distinguish authorization problems from other validation failures.
The console shall distinguish ineligible numbers from other validation failures.
The console shall distinguish duplicate requests from other validation failures.
The console shall indicate whether staff can correct the request themselves or must refer or escalate it.
The console shall point to the exact field or condition causing the issue.
The console shall state what was expected versus what was found.
The console shall provide the next action in plain language when possible.
The console shall present issue messages clearly enough that a user can fix the issue without interpreting a technical error code.
Authorization problems should be escalated to the responsible team.
Eligibility disputes should be escalated to the responsible team.
Cases where the underlying provider data does not match should be escalated to the responsible team.
The administration console shall support search and filtering by phone number, provider, transaction ID, status, date/time, and cutover window.
Before data moves again, the authorized operations lead or responsible integration team must confirm that the channel is fixed or that an approved fallback is in place.
The console can resume the release once the required documentation and approval are completed.
The console shall compare timestamps, transaction sequence, and source authority when evaluating portability state updates.

The system shall allow the transaction to move forward only after the noncompliant interface is restored to approved status or an approved alternate channel is set up and confirmed by the responsible team.
The system shall require documented approval from operations and the integration or network side before clearing the hold.
A temporary fallback for urgent service continuity shall be permitted only in a genuine service-impacting situation where delaying the release would create a customer outage or a regulatory risk.
A temporary fallback for urgent service continuity shall be permitted only if an authorized manager or operations lead approves it.
A temporary fallback for urgent service continuity shall not be used as a routine workaround.
While a temporary fallback for urgent service continuity is in use, the system shall restrict its scope to the specific transaction or data set that needs continuity.
While a temporary fallback for urgent service continuity is in use, the system shall not enable broader automated updates.
The console shall provide an exception queue so staff do not have to search through routine work.
The console shall separate alerts from normal updates very clearly.
The console shall prevent operators from mistaking a temporary override for a standard confirmation.
The console shall display approval history and expiry time on the record.
The exception queue or review panel shall display only items that are blocked, need manual approval, or have an active exception.
The system shall prioritize items first by service impact and urgency.
The system shall prioritize items next by how close they are to their cutover or expiry time.
The system shall prioritize items next by whether they are waiting on the organization or waiting on an external provider.
Some items should be handled separately rather than mixed into the normal exception queue.
Pure informational updates should not sit in the normal exception queue.
Already-closed transactions should not sit in the normal exception queue.
Duplicate notifications should not sit in the normal exception queue.
System health or interface outages should be kept in an operations incident view rather than in the port coordination queue.
Items blocked by a data validation failure should be tagged differently from items blocked by a compliance approval issue.
Staff should be able to distinguish whether a blocked item is a business exception or a technical exception.
A port-coordination item shall be treated as an in-scope exception only if it requires a human decision before the port can continue.
A port-coordination item shall be treated as an in-scope exception only if it requires approval before the port can continue.
A port-coordination item shall be treated as an in-scope exception only if it requires corrective action before the port can continue.
A status feed shall stay out of the exception queue.
A confirmation that has already been fully completed shall stay out of the exception queue.
A message repeating the same transaction state shall stay out of the exception queue.
An authorized supervisor should be able to manually reorder the queue when there is a customer-impact reason.
Manual priority changes should be logged so they are auditable.
The system shall accept an incoming update as the latest state only if it has a clearly newer sequence or timestamp and matches the expected transaction context.
The system shall hold an incoming update for operator review if the timestamps are the same or the sequence is out of order but the content still appears valid.

The system shall reject an incoming update or send it back for reprocessing rather than apply it automatically if it conflicts with the active state in a way that suggests a duplicate, replay, or bad feed from a provider.
A correction to an approved record shall be authorized only by a limited set of privileged users, such as supervisors or designated operations leads, and not by general staff.
Supporting evidence for a correction to an approved record may include a provider notice, an audit reference, or a ticket number.

Migration records that cannot be cleanly mapped to the new portability data shall be placed in a dedicated data-mapping exception queue for manual review by operations staff with provider-domain knowledge.
A supervisor may also review a migration record if the mismatch affects a large batch or a critical customer.
A minor nonessential field mismatch should not prevent cutover, and the issue should be flagged for cleanup.
If the cutover date arrives and a migration record is still unresolved, it shall be kept blocked and escalated immediately rather than forced through with bad data.

The system shall use the risk of incorrect number routing, loss of service, or breach of regulatory or provider agreement obligations as the deciding rule for whether an unresolved mapping issue can be released.
The affected record can be released only with a documented exception if the business owner accepts the risk, the impact is limited, and there is a clear rollback or correction path after cutover.
A documented exception shall only be triggered when the issue is low impact.
A documented exception shall only be triggered when the issue is tightly bounded to a specific record or small batch.
A documented exception shall only be triggered when there is no material risk of wrong routing or service disruption if the system proceeds.
A documented exception shall require a clear compensating control.
A documented exception shall include a planned correction window as an example of a compensating control.
If the business owner is unavailable or declines, approval shall fall to a delegated operations manager or duty executive with the same authority level.
If no delegated operations manager or duty executive with the same authority level is reachable, the item shall remain blocked.
The service management center shall own the synchronization process itself.
Each participating provider shall be responsible for sending timely updates and corrections for the records it controls.
Updated portability data shall be distributed first to the networks directly affected by the change and that need it for routing accuracy.
If a record is under reconciliation or has an open exception, the system shall hold it back from general distribution until the discrepancy is resolved or a formal exception is approved.
A record shall be published in the next normal publish cycle without extra manual review if it is complete, approved, and within the cutover window.
A record shall be delayed if there is a pending validation run.
A record shall be delayed if it depends on another record in the same batch.
A record shall be delayed if the distribution window has already closed for that cycle.
A temporary workaround or manual reconciliation shall be used only if the issue is limited, reversible, and an audit trail can be preserved without changing the underlying business truth.

A temporary workaround may be justified when the mismatch affects live routing, a publish deadline, or a large set of records, and the workaround can be safely isolated to one item with a clear rollback.

A workaround is acceptable without provider confirmation only when the operational risk of waiting is higher than the risk of temporarily handling the issue internally, and the workaround can be clearly marked as provisional.
Controlled changes shall follow a regular release cadence.
An expedited change path shall be allowed only for urgent operational risk.
An expedited change shall be triggered when something is actively hurting service.
A routing defect shall qualify as a trigger for an expedited change.
A compliance deadline shall qualify as a trigger for an expedited change.
A live porting incident that cannot wait for the next cycle shall qualify as a trigger for an expedited change.
A documented impact assessment shall be required before bypassing the normal release cycle.
A clear rollback or fallback plan shall be required before bypassing the normal release cycle.
An issue shall be treated as unable to wait when it is already causing failed port activations.
An issue shall be treated as unable to wait when it is causing incorrect routing.
An issue shall be treated as unable to wait when it is causing a material backlog that is blocking customer moves.
A defect shall be treated as needing immediate handling when it is affecting multiple providers.
A defect shall be treated as needing immediate handling when it has a compliance or service-level deadline within the current cycle.
A defect shall be treated as needing immediate handling when it is getting worse fast.
If an issue is contained, has a safe workaround, and the next release is close enough that the business impact is manageable, the issue should wait for the next release.
The decision threshold is whether delaying the fix creates a bigger operational or customer risk than releasing it early.
The system shall support exception handling.
The system shall support conflict handling.
The system shall support conflict resolution.
The decision to handle an urgent change as an immediate fix shall be based on whether the problem is stopping or corrupting live portability operations right now.
If the issue is causing failed ports, the system shall treat it as an immediate fix.
If the issue is causing wrong routing, the system shall treat it as an immediate fix.
If the issue creates a compliance exposure that cannot be contained, the system shall treat it as an immediate fix.
If the impact is annoying but contained and a workaround preserves correct operation, the system shall defer the change to the next release.
The risk of the fix itself shall be considered when deciding how to handle an urgent change.
If rushing the change is likely to create a bigger outage than the original issue, the system shall use a workaround until it can be released properly.
The system shall record request intake.
The system shall record validation results.
The system shall record status changes.
The system shall record conflicts raised.
The system shall record approvals and overrides.
The system shall record routing activation.
The system shall record retry or cancellation actions.
The system shall record the final outcome.
For post-incident review or routine audit, the recorded history may be available after the live operation is resolved.
The dispute shall only be resolved by designated operations staff with authority over number portability.
For certain cases, an approved escalation owner shall resolve the dispute if the providers cannot agree.
If a conflict affects the correctness of routing or the ownership of the number, work shall pause until the conflict is resolved.
If a conflict is only a documentation mismatch and live routing is still safe, a provisional decision shall allow the process to continue.
If a case touches regulatory obligations or industry-defined rules, escalation shall be required before routing proceeds.
The operating procedure shall define the external escalation path.
Immediate access to porting history shall be available for provider disputes.
Immediate access to porting history shall be available for suspected fraud cases and unauthorized ports.
Immediate access to porting history shall be available for unresolved timeouts that are blocking the transaction.
Staff shall have the full porting trail before taking a manual override or reversal action.
Immediate access to porting history is less critical for a normal completed transaction with no active issue.
The process should pause if the conflict could lead to an illegal port, wrong routing, or customer harm.
The process may continue provisionally only when the risk is low, the routing outcome is still reversible, and there is documented approval to proceed while the escalation is pending.
Provisional continuation of routing work shall be allowed only when the port is operationally safe to proceed.
The port is operationally safe to proceed only when it is not likely to misroute traffic or violate a hard regulatory rule.
Provisional continuation may apply to clerical issues.
Provisional continuation may apply to missing confirmation issues.
Provisional continuation may apply to interpretation questions that can be corrected without changing the live routing outcome.
Staff shall be able to see transaction identifiers.
Staff shall be able to see the provider names involved in the case.
Staff shall not necessarily be shown the full customer profile.
Some fields shall be limited for privacy.
The system shall use role-based access so operations can see what they need.
Unmasking restricted case data shall occur only when the data is genuinely necessary to resolve an active porting issue.
The reason for granting broader access shall be recorded in the case history.
Legacy records shall be retained for as long as business, regulatory, and audit requirements require, with the retention period defined by policy rather than left open-ended.
Access to legacy records shall be tightly restricted to authorized operations, compliance, audit, and support staff, while normal users remain in the new system only.
